ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The electromotive force of the power supply is 3V. The small bulb L is labeled "2V 0.4W". When switch S is connected to 1 and the rheostat is adjusted to $R = 4\Omega$, the small bulb L lights up normally. Now, switch S is connected to 2, and both the small bulb L and the motor M work normally.

1. What is the internal resistance of the power supply?
2. What is the normal operating voltage of the electric motor?
3. What is the approximate power efficiency?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The electromotive force of the power supply is 3V. The small bulb L is labeled "2V 0.4W". When switch S is connected to 1 and the rheostat is adjusted to $R = 4\Omega$, the small bulb L lights up normally. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, on the left is the small light bulb L, and the right end of the bulb is connected to the moving contact of the single-pole double-throw switch S. The upper contact of the switch is labeled 1 and is connected to the sliding rheostat branch at the upper right; the lower contact is labeled 2 and is connected to the motor M branch on the right. The right ends of the sliding rheostat branch and the motor branch both merge into the right-side wire, and together with the power supply below and the bulb on the left form a closed circuit. Therefore, when S is connected to 1, the bulb L and the sliding rheostat are in series; when S is connected to 2, the bulb L and the motor M are in series. Reasoning: The electromotive force of the power supply E=3 V, and the small light bulb is marked “2 V 0.4 W”; when it emits light normally, the current I=P_L/U_L=0.4/2=0.2 A. When S is connected to 1, the sliding rheostat R=4 Ω and the bulb emits light normally, and the series current in the circuit is 0.2 A. Let the internal resistance of the power supply be r, then E=U_L+IR+Ir, that is, 3=2+0.2×4+0.2r, solving gives r=1 Ω. When S is connected to 2, both the bulb and the motor work normally, and the normal current of the bulb is still 0.2 A, so the series circuit current is still 0.2 A. The voltage across the motor U_M=E-U_L-Ir=3-2-0.2×1=0.8 V. The power supply efficiency is calculated according to the ratio of the voltage obtained by the external circuit to the electromotive force: η=(U_L+U_M)/E=(2+0.8)/3≈0.933, that is, about 93.3%.
